questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | GA Question: 1
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Two processes, $P1$ and $P2$, need to access a critical section of code. Consider the following synchronization construct used by the processes:

/*  P1   */
while (true) {
    wants1 = true;
    while (wants2 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants1 = false;
}
/* Remainder section */

/*  P2   */
while (true) {
    wants2 = true;
    while (wants1 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants2=false;
}
/* Remainder section */

Here, wants$1$ and wants$2$ are shared variables, which are initialized to false.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE about the construct?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Two processes, $P1$ and $P2$, need to access a critical section of code. Consider the following synchronization construct used by the processes:

/*  P1   */
while (true) {
    wants1 = true;
    while (wants2 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants1 = false;
}
/* Remainder section */

/*  P2   */
while (true) {
    wants2 = true;
    while (wants1 == true);
    /* Critical Section */
    wants2=false;
}
/* Remainder section */

Here, wants$1$ and wants$2$ are shared variables, which are initialized to false.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE about the construct?

  1. It does not ensure mutual exclusion.

  2. It does not ensure bounded waiting.

  3. It requires that processes enter the critical section in strict alteration.

  4. It does not prevent deadlocks, but ensures mutual exclusion.
options: It does not ensure mutual exclusion.
It does not ensure bounded waiting.
It requires that processes enter the critical section in strict alteration.
It does not prevent deadlocks, but ensures mutual exclusion.

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | GA Question: 2
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Information about a collection of students is given by the relation $\text{studInfo(}\underline{\text{studId}},\text{ name, sex)}$. The relation $\text{enroll(}{\text{studId}},{\text{ courseId}})$ gives which student has enrolled for (or taken) what course(s). Assume that every course is taken by at least one male and at least one female student. What does the following relational algebra expression represent?

$\pi _{courceId}\left(\left(\pi_{\text{studId}}\left(\sigma_{sex=“female"}\left(\text{studInfo}\right)\right) \times \pi_{courseId}\left(\text{enroll}\right)\right) -\text{enroll}\right)$

  1. Courses in which all the female students are enrolled.
  2. Courses in which a proper subset of female students are enrolled.
  3. Courses in which only male students are enrolled.
  4. None of the above

questions.question:

$\left\{e.name \mid employee(e) \wedge \left(\forall x\right)\left[\neg employee\left(x \right) \vee x.supervisorName \neq e.name \vee x.sex = ``male" \right]\right\}$

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | GA Question: 7
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Hari(H), Gita(G), Irfan(I) and Saira(S) are siblings (i.e., brothers and sisters). All were born on $1^{\text{st}}$ January. The age difference between any two successive siblings (that is born one after another) is less than three years. Given the following facts:

  1. Hari's age $+$ Gita's age $>$ Irfan's age $+$ Saira's age
  2. The age difference between Gita and Saira is one year. However Gita is not the oldest and Saira is not the youngest.
  3. There are no twins.

In what order they were born (oldest first)?

questions.question: Maxwell's divergence equation $\nabla \cdot \vec{B} = 0$ physically asserts that:

Electric field is conservative in static conditions
Magnetic flux changes induce an electromotive force
Total charge inside a closed volume is conserved

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Magnetic flux changes induce an electromotive force
structuredOptions.html: Magnetic flux changes induce an electromotive force

structuredOptions.label: D

structuredOptions.html: Total charge inside a closed volume is conserved

$\nabla \cdot \vec{B} = 0$ states that magnetic flux lines are always continuous closed loops, proving that isolated single magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist.

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | EE Question: 8
questions.subject: Signals & Systems
questions.question: A continuous-time LTI system with impulse response $h(t) = e^{-2t} u(t)$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Signals & Systems):

Causality: $h(t) = 0$ for $t < 0$ due to $u(t)$. Stability: $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} |h(t)| dt = \int_0^\infty e^{-2t} dt = \left[-\frac{e^{-2t}}{2}\right]_0^\infty = \frac{1}{2} < \infty$. Hence both causal and BIBO stable.

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | EE Question: 26
questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The open-loop transfer function of a unity feedback system is $G(s) = \frac{K}{s(s+2)(s+4)}$. Using Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion, the maximum value of $K$ for closed-loop stability is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

Characteristic equation: $1 + G(s) = 0 \implies s(s^2 + 6s + 8) + K = 0 \implies s^3 + 6s^2 + 8s + K = 0$. Routh array first column entries: $s^3: 1$, $s^2: 6$, $s^1: \frac{6(8) - K}{6} = \frac{48 - K}{6}$, $s^0: K$. For stability, all terms must be positive: $48 - K > 0 \implies K < 48$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | EE Question: 31
questions.subject: Power Electronics & Drives
questions.question: A single-phase full-wave controlled bridge rectifier is fed from a $230\text{ V}$ (RMS), $50\text{ Hz}$ AC source. The firing angle is $\alpha = 60^\circ$. Assuming continuous conduction, the average DC output voltage $V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \cos \alpha$ (in Volts) is ________ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Electronics & Drives):

$V_m = 230 \times \sqrt{2} = 325.27\text{ V}$. $V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \cos(60^\circ) = \frac{2 \times 325.27}{\pi} \times 0.5 = \frac{325.27}{3.1416} = 103.54\text{ V}$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | EE Question: 38
questions.subject: Analog & Digital Electronics
questions.question: An ideal op-amp in inverting amplifier configuration has input resistance $R_1 = 10\,\text{k}\Omega$ and feedback resistance $R_f = 100\,\text{k}\Omega$. If input voltage is $V_{\text{in}} = 0.5\text{ V}$, the output voltage $V_{\text{out}} = -\frac{R_f}{R_1} V_{\text{in}}$ (in Volts) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Analog & Digital Electronics):

Inverting voltage gain $A_v = -\frac{R_f}{R_1} = -\frac{100}{10} = -10$. Output $V_{\text{out}} = -10 \times 0.5\text{ V} = -5.0\text{ V}$.
